channel.title: 3FS Rural Home blog
channel.description: Plain-English guides to USDA rural home loans.

item.title: What is a USDA home loan, and who is it for?
item.description: A USDA home loan helps people buy or build in rural areas, often with no down payment. Here is who it is for, the two kinds, and the three things you need.

item.title: USDA income limits for 2026: how to read them and where most of the country lands
item.description: FY2026 USDA income limits explained. 2,065 of 2,724 areas share the same $122,800 Guaranteed limit for a family of four; higher-cost metros go up from there. How household size changes it.

item.title: USDA Direct vs Guaranteed loans: which one is yours?
item.description: The difference between a USDA Direct loan (USDA lends, for lower incomes, with payment assistance) and a Guaranteed loan (a lender lends, USDA backs it). How to tell which one fits your income.

item.title: How young adults are buying a first home with no down payment
item.description: A step-by-step path for a young adult or young family to buy a first home with a USDA loan and no down payment: what to check, what to gather, who to call, and what to expect.

item.title: How to tell if an address is in a USDA eligible area
item.description: What "rural" means for USDA loans, why towns up to about 35,000 people can qualify, how to read the area type on the 3FS map, and how to confirm an exact address on USDA's eligibility site.

item.title: For builders: where USDA buyers are, and how to plan homes for them
item.description: How home builders use USDA Guaranteed and Direct loans to sell new homes in rural and exurban areas: find qualifying buyers by ZIP, overlap Opportunity Zones, and build to USDA's modest-home standard.
